title: The Amazing Adventures of Coffee Man!
statementMd:
By day, Coffee Man is an ordinary office worker. But give him a cup of coffee and he becomes a superhero who can leap across the city in a single bound!

Coffee Man is standing at point $0$ of a number line, and he needs to get to point $n$ (reaching any point with coordinate at least $n$ is enough). He brought $m$ cups of coffee; the $i$-th cup initially has temperature $a_i$.

Every second, Coffee Man does exactly one of the following:

- **walk**: his coordinate increases by $1$;
- **drink** a cup he has not drunk yet: his coordinate increases by the current temperature of that cup.

Each cup can be drunk at most once. Unfortunately, coffee gets cold: after every second, the temperature of every cup decreases by $1$, but it never goes below $0$. In other words, if Coffee Man drinks the $i$-th cup when exactly $s$ seconds have passed, he moves forward by $\max(0, a_i - s)$.

What is the minimum number of seconds Coffee Man needs to reach a point with coordinate at least $n$?

## Input

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $t$ ($1 \le t \le 10^4$). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case contains two integers $n$ and $m$ ($1 \le n \le 10^9$, $1 \le m \le 2 \cdot 10^5$) — the coordinate Coffee Man needs to reach and the number of cups of coffee.

The second line of each test case contains $m$ integers $a_1, a_2, \ldots, a_m$ ($1 \le a_i \le 10^9$) — the initial temperatures of the cups.

It is guaranteed that the sum of $m$ over all test cases does not exceed $2 \cdot 10^5$.

## Output

For each test case, output a single integer — the minimum number of seconds Coffee Man needs to reach a point with coordinate at least $n$.

## Note

In the first test case, $n = 10$ and the temperatures are $[1, 3, 5]$. One optimal plan is:

- second $1$: drink the cup with temperature $5$, moving to coordinate $5$;
- second $2$: drink the cup that started at temperature $3$; it has cooled to $2$, so Coffee Man moves to coordinate $7$;
- seconds $3$, $4$, $5$: walk, reaching coordinate $10$.

It is not possible to do better, so the answer is $5$. Note that drinking all three cups in the given order is worse: the cups give $1$, $2$ and $3$, so after $3$ seconds Coffee Man is at coordinate $6$ and needs $4$ more seconds of walking, $7$ seconds in total.

In the second test case, a single cup moves Coffee Man from $0$ to $100 \ge 3$.

In the third test case, the cups are useless: the first one moves him by $1$, which is no better than walking, and after that every cup has cooled down to $0$. The answer is $5$.

In the fourth test case, drinking all four cups gives $4+3+2+1=10$ units of movement in four seconds, after which walking takes ten more seconds. The total is $14$ seconds.
